JUDGEMENT CALLS:
  S6 (816,468) = CROSSING. The D4->D10 column draws an unmistakable semicircular/S hop around the +5V rail (hop score 3.6, plainly visible in the site crop). Reading it as a junction would merge D4's cathode and D10's anode into the +5V rail, shorting both diodes to the supply and collapsing n5.
  S5 (881,467) = JUNCTION. Plain X, no dot, no hop, sitting 65 px from S6 where the same drafter drew an obvious hop - so a bare crossing here is deliberate ink for 'connected'. The alternative (crossing) would separate {+5V, R8 right} from {Q2 emitter, Q13 emitter, Q19 collector}, leaving the +5V source feeding nothing but one resistor end and the whole right-hand output column with no supply.
  S9 (424,486) = JUNCTION. Plain X where the +6V arrow's stem passes the R9/R8 rail on its way down to Q12's emitter. Same drafter habit, and it matches the way +15V lands on the top rail (S0) and +10V lands between R1 and R5 (S2). Crossing would give +6V only to Q12's emitter and leave the R9-R8 midpoint as an isolated 2-terminal node.
  S24 (529,776) = CROSSING. R16's bottom lead makes a distinct sideways S-jog exactly where it meets the horizontal wire - visible in the S24 crop and again, from below, in the S31 crop. Junction would put R16's bottom AND Q12's collector AND Q20's collector AND Q18's base all on GND: Q20 would have collector shorted to emitter and Q18 would have base = emitter = 0, i.e. two transistors stranded dead and R16 with one end shorted to the node it is supposed to bias from. The crossing reading gives R16 bottom -> GND (a base bleed for Q12) and Q12/Q20 collectors -> Q18 base, which mirrors stage 4 exactly (Q18 collector -> Q13 base).
  S0 (554,216), S2 (244,321), S7 (224,486), S8 (802,484), S10 (889,594), S12 (802,612), S13 (47,626), S17 (410,716), S26 (127,806), S27 (893,816), S28 (207,819), S29 (670,819), S30 (407,820), S31 (517,820) = JUNCTION. All are plain T's - a lead or a supply-arrow stem ending on a through wire - so there is nothing to pass through.
  S15/S16/S18/S20 (x 60..106, y ~717) are strokes of the handwritten '50k ohm' label brushing R17; left at the default, they touch no terminal after the R17 port fix.

PORT / PIN FIXES:
  Q11, Q12, Q13, Q15 (BJT-PNP): pin order rebuilt as (collector, base, emitter). In all four the base is the lead on the far side of the vertical base bar (left for Q11/Q13/Q15, right for Q12) and the emitter carries the arrowhead pointing back into the base bar; that emitter lead is in every case the one running to the more positive node (n6, n7, n4, n10 respectively), and the remaining lead runs toward ground. The tracer had the base on the wrong pin for Q13 and emitter/collector swapped on Q11, Q12 and Q15.
  Q18 (BJT-NPN): the tracer put t0 on the base wire, t1 on a stray piece of the ground rail at (631,818) and t2 on the emitter. Corrected to base = p0 (629,771) -> t1, emitter = p1 (670,807) -> t2. The collector lead leaves the box top at ~(668,744) and no port was generated for it, so t0 is asserted with manual_nets = n8: the lead runs up to (668,732) and east to (770,734), where the ink stops 3 px short of the n8 column (pixel dump at x[764,809) y[712,757) shows the horizontal ending at x=793, y=736-737 and the column occupying x=796-799 down to y=735). That is a pen gap in a single drawn corner, not a break - nothing else in the drawing could terminate that wire.
  R17 (50k, bottom left): terminal 1 was sitting on a stroke of the handwritten '50k ohm' label at (66,733) (wire length 10 px), which is what produced the 1-terminal net n13 in the tracer's output. Repointed to p3 (40,767), the real bottom lead, which runs down to (40,806) on the ground rail.
  Unused port candidates left alone: #3 p1 (177,278) is the +10V arrowhead, #8 p2 (589,505) is a stroke of the '15k ohm' label - both correctly not used as terminals.

CLASSES: all accepted as annotated. D4 and D10 are both drawn as a downward-pointing triangle with a cathode bar; D4's bar has a small hook on its left end that could be read as a Zener marker, but D10 - drawn in the same hand, same size, same left-end thickening - is unambiguously a plain diode, so I kept both as Diode rather than reclassifying one.
